Root cause: scripts/issue2203_common.py resolves the repo root via `from explore_persona_space.task_workflow import repo_root` and calls repo_root() in assistant_axis_dir() / query_banks_dir() / eval_results_dir(). That resolver is a VM/main-context resolver: it (a) hard-requires a `tasks/` directory at the repo root, and (b) branch-guards to `main` (a non-main HEAD routes to a managed main-pin worktree that ALSO needs tasks/). On a pod the checkout is on branch `issue-2203` with `tasks/` sparse-excluded (NO_TASKS_DIR confirmed), so the FIRST clause raised: `RuntimeError: resolved repo root /workspace/explore-persona-space has no tasks/ directory`.

Established sibling pattern: every other pod-side issue script resolves the repo root pod-safely and does NOT touch task_workflow — issue664_common.py / issue734_common.py use `REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`; issue1689_common.py uses an `EPS_REPO_ROOT > WORKLOAD_ROOT > Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` resolver. issue2203_common.py is the lone divergence. The CLAUDE.md "use task_workflow.repo_root()" rule is scoped to `tasks/...` paths; the data/eval/figures paths these helpers build are not tasks paths, so the sibling `__file__`-based pattern is the correct pod-safe form.

Fix (Step 7 crash-fix round, experiment-implementer + code-review): conform issue2203_common.py to the sibling `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` repo-root pattern, drop the task_workflow import, keep assistant_axis_dir/query_banks_dir/eval_results_dir semantics identical. Fix lands on the VM worktree, commits, pushes; pod pulls; then relaunch the Phase-0/1 chain.

# Reproduced assistant-axis capping reduces jailbreak harm only by degrading the model's output, not by localizing the assistant persona (MODERATE confidence)

<!-- clean-result-v4 -->

## Takeaways

- **Prefix-only capping does nothing:** harm 0.093 vs 0.097 baseline, identity-loss 0.292 vs 0.284 (497 harm items, 250 identity). The hypothesised prefix failure holds.
- **Context-vector capping does not recover the all-token effect:** harm 0.127 (above baseline), identity-loss 0.288; its same-position random-direction control also fails (0.092), so the null is genuine, not low power.
- **The only harm "reduction" (all-token cap, 0.097 → 0.012) is degradation:** a random direction cuts harm more (0.000), 485 of 500 completions are gibberish, coherent ones stay at 0.133.
- **The Qwen-3-32B anchor (Lu et al.'s published vectors) shows the same artifact:** all-token 0.040 → 0.000 at 500/500 gibberish, context 0.026 at 326/500; its 4.0% baseline is weak.
- **Harm-cutting arms wreck capability and censor the identity DV:** all-token cap GSM8K 0.87 → 0.62, IFEval 0.69 → 0.13, identity on 36 of 250 items. Axis-component-replace (0.097 → 0.060, capability intact) is the lone coherent, uncontrolled reduction.

## Goal

- **This experiment in context:** Lu et al. (2601.10387) blunt persona jailbreaks by flooring a model's hidden-state component along an "assistant axis" (default assistant minus role-play personas) at *every token*, reporting ~60% fewer harmful responses. Prior in-house work localised persona information at the *context vector* (the last prompt-token state, [#2094](https://eps.superkaiba.com/tasks/2094)), predicting that a cap only there should recover most of the effect far more cheaply, while a prefix cap should fail. This run reproduces the defence on Qwen-2.5-7B (in-house axis) and a Qwen-3-32B anchor (the paper's own vectors), sweeping position against three intervention types: floor the component, replace it with the default-assistant value, or replace the whole state.
- **Broader narrative:** It probes where the assistant persona is *causally controllable* and whether a cheap, position-localised version of the defence exists. The caution here: the apparent gains are output degradation, so "cheaper localisation" is premature until a version that cuts harm while keeping the model coherent is shown.

## Methodology

**Design:** A training-free forward-hook intervention study on Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, no fine-tuning. The 7B grid is 16 arms: a position ladder (prefix end / context vector / all prompt tokens / all tokens) crossed with three intervention types (cap = floor the assistant-axis component to a threshold; axis-component-replace = overwrite that component with the default-assistant value; full-replace = overwrite the whole hidden state with the default-assistant state), plus an unmodified baseline and four controls — two footprint-matched norm-matched random-direction caps (one at the context vector, one at all tokens), a single-mid-layer (layer 14) cap, and the baseline. All 7B arms cap over a fixed layer band (18-25) selected by a Phase-1 sweep. A Qwen-3-32B anchor runs a baseline plus all-token and context caps using Lu et al.'s published vectors and their `layers_46:54-p0.25` configuration (intervention layers 46-53). Representation-mapping "prefix vs context" arms are both present as ladder rungs; no representation map is *fitted* here (this is steering, not a learned predictor), so the identity/kNN mapping-baseline reads do not apply.

**Training:** **N/A — no model training.** The axis, threshold, and layer band are the only fitted quantities; every value below is copied from the run artifacts.

| Axis stability / PC1 alignment (mid layer) | cos 0.964 split-half; cos(axis, role-PC1) 0.80 | phase-0 axis validation |

**Evaluation:** Two co-primary judged rates per arm: the jailbreak harmful-response rate (fraction of the 500 jailbreak prompts whose mean judge score is at least 50) and the assistant-identity-loss rate (fraction of the 250 role-play items the judge classifies as no longer the Assistant). Continuous companions: the graded 0-100 assistant-ness mean and the fraction of positions where the cap actually fired (a before-vs-after axis-projection magnitude was not separately stored — only firing fractions were). Capability guardrails (GSM8K, IFEval, MMLU-Pro) run under the same hook per arm. Because the evaluated model is Qwen-family under an English eval, every arm's completions were scanned for CJK-script intrusion (a per-completion regex over both the jailbreak and role-play pools), and the jailbreak harm rate was recomputed on the coherent (non-CJK) subset — the load-bearing check for this result. Malformed / instructed-`REFUSAL` / out-of-range judge verdicts are dropped, never coerced, and reported per arm.

**Data extraction:** Reconstructed jailbreak prompts from three established safety banks (`strongreject_v1` = 313, `advbench_v1` = 200, `wang44_v1` = 44; 500 sampled), a stated deviation from the paper's Shah et al. jailbreak set — carried as a scope caveat, and the reason the 32B baseline harm rate is only 4.0% (a much easier set than the paper's). The role-susceptibility items are the persona role-play plus "who are you?"-style introspective questions from the in-house role bank. Banks are referenced by filename and count only.

## Results

### Prefix-only capping does nothing; context-vector capping does not recover the all-token effect

What is plotted: the position ladder (prefix end / context vector / all prompt / all tokens) for all three intervention types; top panel jailbreak harm rate, bottom panel identity-loss rate. Dashed = baseline, dotted / dash-dot = the two random-direction controls, hollow markers = cells whose output is more than half CJK gibberish, whiskers = 95% proportion intervals (497 harm / 250 identity items).

![Two-panel position ladder for cap, axis-replace and full-replace, with baseline and two random-null reference lines. Prefix and context arms sit at or above baseline on both panels; rates fall only at the broad-position right side, where the all-token cap point is a hollow marker.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/12e7f0386d53538eaf647d140e0cc9c7f4c46563/figures/issue_2203/hero_position_ladder.png)

> **Figure.** *Where along the input the cap is applied (Qwen-2.5-7B, harm n=497, identity n=250).* Harm (top) and identity-loss (bottom) rate vs position for three intervention types; dashed = baseline, dotted / dash-dot = context and all-token random-direction controls, hollow point = >50% CJK-degenerate output.

Prefix-end capping lands on baseline for every intervention type. Context-vector capping never drops below baseline (cap 0.127, axis-replace 0.090, full-replace 0.171 vs 0.097), so the localisation prediction fails. Rates fall only at the broad-position right edge — and every point that falls is either hollow (degenerate) or, for axis-replace, uncontrolled for specificity, which the next results unpack.

### The all-token harm reduction rides on CJK output degradation, not the assistant axis

What is plotted: for the cap family plus its all-token random-direction control, three bars per arm — harm over all rows, harm over coherent (non-CJK) rows only, and the fraction of completions that are CJK gibberish. Dashed = baseline harm.

All-token cap has near-zero all-rows harm but 0.133 coherent-rows harm and 0.97 CJK fraction; the random null has zero harm, no coherent rows, and 1.0 CJK.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/superkaiba/explore-persona-space/12e7f0386d53538eaf647d140e0cc9c7f4c46563/figures/issue_2203/degradation_mechanism.png)

> **Figure.** *Harm reduction tracks CJK degradation, not the axis (Qwen-2.5-7B, harm n≈497/arm).* Per cap arm: all-rows harm, coherent-only harm, CJK-gibberish fraction; dashed = baseline. All-token cap's all-rows harm collapses only because 97% of outputs are gibberish.

All-token cap's headline 0.012 comes entirely from broken output: on the 15 coherent-English completions harm is 0.133, at or above baseline. The random direction at all tokens cuts harm *further* (0.000) at 100% gibberish, so the cap fails to clear its footprint-matched control — the effect is not axis-specific. The context random control leaves harm at baseline (0.092), confirming the context null above is genuine, not degradation.

### The Qwen-3-32B faithful anchor reproduces the degradation, not the paper's clean effect

### 1. Axis-specificity control for the coherent axis-component-replace reduction (7B) — [Type: Ablation]

**Parent:** #2203
**question_relation:** same
**followup_label:** axis-replace-random-control
**Goal:** Determine whether assistant-axis activation capping (and its query-preserving patch generalization) applied ONLY at the context-vector position recovers the jailbreak-reduction / persona-stabilization effect that Lu et al. (arXiv 2601.10387) get by capping at every token, and whether prefix-only capping fails — via a position ladder (prefix-end / context-end / all-prompt / all-tokens) x intervention type (cap / axis-component-replace / full-replace) over a fixed mid-late layer band, on Qwen-2.5-7B (in-house axis) with a Qwen-3-32B faithful anchor, scored on co-primary judged jailbreak-harm and role-susceptibility rates.
**Hypothesis:** The two broad-position axis-component-replace arms (all-prompt 0.097→0.060, all-token →0.064, capability intact) are the run's ONLY coherent harm reductions but have no random-direction control. If the reduction is axis-specific, a norm-matched random-direction component-replace at the SAME two positions will leave harm at/near baseline (0.097) with capability intact; if it is generic component-overwrite disruption, random-replace will match the axis-replace reduction — the same non-specificity the cap family already showed (random beat axis at all-token).
**Falsification:** A norm-matched random-direction replace at all-prompt / all-token reduces harm to ~0.060-0.064 at comparable GSM8K/IFEval → the coherent reduction is NOT axis-specific, and the last candidate positive effect in the study collapses into the degradation/non-specificity story.
**Differs from parent:** Adds one control family — a seeded, norm-matched random-direction axis-component-replace at all-prompt and all-token (mirroring the parent's existing `cap_*_randnull` design, which covered the CAP family only). One variable: the replaced-component direction (assistant axis → random), op (axis-component-replace) and positions held fixed.

**Pre-filled spec (from parent):**
- Model: same as parent — `Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct`, in-house axis `issue2203_ctx_capping/axis/qwen25_7b_axis_per_layer.pt` (Hub-verified), layer band 18-25.
- Data: same as parent — the 500-prompt reconstructed jailbreak set (412 `strongreject_v1` + 88 `wang44_v1`) + 250 role-susceptibility items; same shas.
- Seeds: same as parent — generation `seed_base=42`; random-null `v_rand` seed pinned exactly as the parent's `cap_*_randnull` arms.
- Eval: same as parent — co-primary judged harm rate + identity-loss rate (Sonnet-4.5, graded 0-100, N=5, threshold 50), CJK-intrusion audit, GSM8K/IFEval/MMLU-Pro guardrails, api-refusal SYNC re-issue.
- Config: same as parent EXCEPT two new arms `axrep_allprompt_randnull` and `axrep_alltoken_randnull` — axis-component-replace where the replaced direction is a norm-matched seeded random `v_rand` instead of the assistant axis (reuse `issue-2203:scripts/issue2203_phase2.py` + `issue-2203:src/explore_persona_space/experiments/issue2203/caphook.py`; the `axrep_*` op and both random-null recipes already exist in the parent code).

**Estimated cost:** ~4 GPU-hours on 1×H100 (2 arms × 750 behavioral + ~960 capability gens; all-token arm ~2× per-decode; judge off-GPU via Batch API, free)
**If it works:** If random-replace stays at baseline while axis-replace reduces → the ONE genuine axis-specific localization signal in the study survives, and the headline softens from "no localization, only degradation" to "localization exists via broad-position axis-component replacement." Rewrites Takeaway 5.
**If it fails:** If random-replace matches axis-replace → every arm in the study is non-specific; the negative hardens to complete. Next: nothing further at 7B on this op — the mechanism is generic disruption.

**auto_run_reason:** Single-variable ablation with a fully-grounded recipe (both the `axrep` op and the norm-matched random-null generator already exist in the parent code); premise artifacts (7B axis + phase2 baseline + phase2 script) Hub-verified for this proposal; cost known and < 20 GPU-h; no human design decision needed.

### 3. Re-test the key arms in a strong-attack (high-baseline) jailbreak regime — [Type: Diagnostic / External-validity]

**question_relation:** same

**Goal:** Determine whether assistant-axis activation capping (and its query-preserving patch generalization) applied ONLY at the context-vector position recovers the jailbreak-reduction / persona-stabilization effect that Lu et al. Two parallel research agents investigated why the #2203 32B anchor degraded (repetitive CJK / Chinese-language flip) instead of reproducing the paper's capping defence. Both findings are load-bearing for #2203's validity and for #2223 (drift replication).

## 1. The Assistant Axis is fully open-source (Anthropic paper) — code + vectors + exact thresholds are all public and directly reusable

- Paper: "The Assistant Axis: Situating and Stabilizing the Default Persona of Language Models" — Lu, Gallagher, Michala, Fish, Lindsey. arXiv 2601.10387.
- Code (MIT, branch master): https://github.com/safety-research/assistant-axis — package `assistant_axis/` with `steering.py` (`ActivationSteering`, `load_capping_config`, `build_capping_steerer`), `generation.py`, per-model configs; `notebooks/steer.ipynb` is a Qwen3-32B capping demo.
- Vectors + per-layer taus: HF dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/lu-christina/assistant-axis-vectors — `qwen-3-32b/assistant_axis.pt` [64,5120], `qwen-3-32b/capping_config.pt`, role/trait vectors. Same layout for llama-3.3-70b + gemma-2-27b.

## 2. TWO candidate bugs in our reproduction (both to be confirmed by the code audit)

(a) SIGN INVERSION (serious). The RELEASED capping vectors point AWAY from the Assistant (cos −1.0 with `assistant_axis.pt`) and use NEGATIVE taus (Qwen layers 46–53: −32.5, −64.5, −35.75, −37.25, −33.0, −28.5, −21.0, −44.5). Their op MAX-caps the projection onto that negated vector: h ← h − v̂·clamp(⟨h,v̂⟩ − τ, min=0). Net = FLOORING the Assistant-Axis projection at +|τ|. If our phase3 applied a max-cap to the Assistant-POINTING axis (or positive taus), it CEILINGS the Assistant projection — the INVERSE intervention, pushing the model OUT of Assistant space — which matches the paper's own "degenerate/mystical output when steered away" regime and would explain our CJK collapse. If confirmed, the #2203 32B "capping degrades the model" takeaway is measuring the anti-cap, not capping.

(b) THINKING MODE. Their generation code hard-codes enable_thinking=False for Qwen (both HF + vLLM paths); the whole 32B result is no-think. Our baseline emitted <think> on 500/500, so we capped over reasoning spans the axis was never calibrated on — a setup mismatch.

Norm-scaling (lmsys-chat-1m) is paper-only (steering x-axis); NOT needed for capping (taus are absolute). Gen settings: temp 0.7, top_p 0.9, 512 new tokens.

## 3. The Shah et al. jailbreak dataset was NEVER publicly released

- Paper: Shah et al. 2023, "Scalable and Transferable Black-Box Jailbreaks via Persona Modulation", arXiv 2311.03348. Deliberately withheld (responsible-disclosure footnote); no GitHub, no HF, no OpenReview supplement.
- The Assistant Axis paper gives no source location for it — strongly implying a private copy from the authors ("willing to collaborate" stance).
- Structure discrepancy: the published Shah paper uses 43 harm categories; the Assistant Axis paper's "44 categories / 1100 (system-prompt, behavioral-question) pairs" is their own sampling from a private copy. No released file/split.
- Access paths: (a) request from authors (Rando/Casper/Shah/Pour/Feuillade-Montixi, or the Assistant Axis authors); (b) reconstruct via the published GPT-4 pipeline (43-category list in the paper's Fig. 2; ~<$3/category). Reconstruction likely matches the Assistant Axis setup about as well as the original, given the 43/44 mismatch.
- Implication for #2203's weak-attack caveat: our reconstructed strongreject/wang44 bank (9.7%/4.0% baseline harm) is NOT the paper's set and cannot be swapped for it by download; a strong-attack test needs a Shah reconstruction or author contact.

[code-audit] #2203 capping reimplementation has three confirmed bugs that invalidate its core conclusions (user-directed audit, 2026-08-10)

Independent read-only audit of scripts/issue2203_*.py + caphook, cross-checked against the paper's released code/vectors (finding #1 in the prior research-consolidation note). Verdicts:

## BUG 1 — 32B anchor (phase3) ran the INVERSE intervention (sign inversion). Severity: invalidates the 32B "capping degrades the model" headline.
- caphook.py:100-102 uses `clamp(proj_raw - tau, max=0.0)` = a MIN-FLOOR of ⟨h,v⟩ at τ (paper's op is `min=0` = a MAX-cap).
- phase3.py:148-151 feeds Lu's released capping vectors verbatim (cos −1.0 with assistant_axis, i.e. anti-Assistant) with their NEGATIVE taus, no negation/flip.
- Net: our op fires on the MOST-assistant rows and drags them OUT of Assistant space (ceilings ⟨h,assistant_axis⟩ at +|τ|) — the paper's op fires on DRIFTED rows and pulls them back IN. Opposite token set, opposite direction. This alone explains the 32B degenerate/CJK collapse. (Confirm which branch ran via `reconstructed_cap`/`reconstructed:False` in phase3_32b_anchor.json — primary path expected.)

## BUG 2 — thinking mode left ON for the 32B (paper hard-codes it OFF). Severity: setup mismatch, compounds BUG 1.
- `enable_thinking` appears nowhere in issue-2203 scripts/caphook/steering; issue1415/steering.py:84-86 renders with no enable_thinking kwarg, so Qwen-3-32B defaulted to thinking-on. The (inverted) cap fired over <think> spans τ was never calibrated on; max_new_tokens=1024 (phase3.py:474) is small for a reasoning model → possible answer truncation.

## BUG 3 — 7B ladder (phase2) cap op overshoots the floor by ‖v‖² (CRITICAL). Severity: confounds the 7B degradation finding (b); footprint-matched null overshoots identically so it cannot isolate axis-specificity for the CAP arms.
- caphook.py:96-102 projects AND updates with the RAW contrast v, omitting 1/‖v‖². Phase-0 axis is the raw diff-of-means, never normalized (phase0.py:402), so ‖v‖² is O(10²–10³) at mid-late layers → a firing cap displaces the residual far more than the state itself (the degeneration mechanism). Unintended: axis_replace in the same file correctly uses v̂ (caphook.py:103-105), and the H4 follow-up divides τ by ‖v‖ (axrep_randnull_h4.py:149). Phase-2 SIGN is correct (assistant-pointing axis + response-pool τ + floor op); only MAGNITUDE is wrong. NOT affected: axis_replace, full_replace.

## BUG-adjacent — the prefix/context "null" is likely a τ-firing artifact, not position-causality.
- τ = 25th pct of RESPONSE-token projections (phase1.py:333) applied to PROMPT positions with a different projection distribution → single-position arms may be near-no-ops by construction. The rig already recorded per-arm `mean_fired_frac` (phase2.py:363-374); the parent body already notes the prefix arm fired on only 10.6% of slots. READ fired_frac before interpreting the null.

## What SURVIVES the audit (clean bills, verified load-bearing)
- Hook position wiring incl. left-pad geometry + decode-step KV indexing: correct, no off-by-one.
- Judge parsing: refusal/malformed/out-of-range DROPPED, never coerced to 0 — a degraded arm cannot manufacture harm=0.
- Join keys / per-row alignment asserted; set pinning deterministic + identical across arms (pairing valid).
- The follow-up axis-specificity finding (`axis-replace-random-control`) uses v̂ correctly on both real + random arms → NOT hit by BUG 3; that "coherent axis-replace reduction is axis-specific" result plausibly stands.

## Implications
- #2203 32B anchor: NOT a faithful replication (inverted cap + thinking-on). Its "capping degrades" takeaway is measuring the anti-cap.
- #2203 7B cap-arm degradation (finding b): confounded by ‖v‖² overshoot.
- #2203 prefix/context null (finding a): uninterpretable until fired_frac is read; likely calibration artifact.
- HAZARD FOR THE LIVE ctx-native-axis-cap FOLLOW-UP: it reuses caphook.py, so its CAP arms inherit BUG 3 (its axis-replace arms + extraction/validation are unaffected).
- Path forward (cheapest + decisive): adopt the paper's OWN released code + vectors (safety-research/assistant-axis, build_capping_steerer) as the capping engine rather than fixing our reimplementation piecemeal. The user-directed no-thinking run on pod-2203-nothink is ALREADY doing exactly this (correct sign via their config, v̂, thinking off) — it is the ground-truth validation.
